priceSnapshot.note: THE OVERNIGHT SLIDE CONTINUED AND MIDNIGHT'S SHORT WAS PAID. Midnight stamped 64,050.0 at 02:20 COT with a range-bear call and opened a small 24 USDT hedge short with targets at 63,889 and 63,611. Price ground straight down through the first: the ledger auto-resolved the position at TP 63,889 and the low since that snapshot is 63,610.6, printed on the 15m bar that opened 06:20 COT (2026-07-31T11:20Z) - a whisker inside the second target the trade never got to use. Price has since bounced 198 points to 63,808.7. Session range measured from the midnight snapshot is 63,610.6 - 64,063.4, a 0.71% band - unusually tight for a tape carrying a 2.56% daily ATR, which is what a market coiling above a large liquidation shelf looks like.

reduceIf.confirmation: Unchanged for a tenth consecutive session and it has still never fired: a 4H CLOSE below $63,000 is what confirms the range break and takes the long-term spot core down a real notch. The live, non-structural line is now $64,063 - today's session high, which also sits just under the 1H EMA20 at 64,200. Below 64,063 every bounce is a retest from below; a 4H close above the 4H EMA50 at $64,425 would cancel the bearish tilt outright.

addIf.confirmation: The next tranche of the long-term core goes to work if price tags the 1.16M CoinGlass liquidation shelf at $63,529 and then reclaims it - specifically a 15m close back above $63,700 after the tag. That is the single heaviest band on the whole 48h map, 6.7x heavier than anything above spot, so a flush into it that immediately reverses is the highest-quality dip this range has offered. A small 6 USDT tranche has ALREADY been deployed at 63,808.7 this session; this rail governs the next one.

liquidation.note: THE DOMINANT FEATURE OF THE MAP AND THE REASON THIS REPORT KEEPS A BEARISH TILT INSIDE A RANGE CALL. Liquidation Leverage reads 1.16M on the CoinGlass 48h Model-3 heatmap, taken from the tooltip at the 2026-07-31 06:30 column. That is the exact maximum of the chart's own colour scale (the legend tops out at 1.16M), so this is the brightest band on the entire two-day surface. It is 6.7x heavier than the nearest band above spot (174.09K at 64,320) and 1.9x heavier than the next shelf below it. It sits 0.44% under spot, which one ordinary hour of drift reaches.

618.00K, the second shelf below and 0.78% under spot. This is the level a genuine break of the 63,529 magnet runs to, and it is why the resting spot stop stays at 63,200 rather than anywhere tighter - 63,200 sits underneath BOTH this shelf and the 63,393 4H EMA200, so a normal sweep of the magnet cannot reach it.

458.66K, 1.34% under spot and just below the $63,000 structural reduce rail. If price is trading here the rail has broken and the reduce is already confirmed; the cluster explains why a break of 63,000 would likely overshoot rather than stall neatly at the round number.

MEASURED DEAD ZONE: Liquidation Leverage reads exactly 0 at this price, 0.10% under spot. There is nothing for price to grab between here and the 63,529 magnet, which is the mechanical argument for why a probe lower would travel fast rather than grind.

liquidityMagnet.note: The pull is DOWN and it is not close. 1.16M sitting 0.44% below spot against 174.09K sitting 0.80% above is a 6.7:1 imbalance, and the 0.10% immediately below spot is a measured dead zone (leverage exactly 0 at 63,744.8) so there is no friction on the way into it. Read this as gravity, not as a forecast: magnets tell you where price is likely to be drawn, not that it must break. The honest expression of that is a bearish TILT inside a range call plus a small spot add rather than a leveraged short into a 0.44% target.

atr.source: Computed here (Wilder ATR-14) from Kraken XBTUSDT daily OHLC over 43 sessions through the in-progress 2026-07-31 UTC candle, seeded on a 14-bar simple average of true range and then Wilder-smoothed for the remaining bars. Math: TR = max(H-L, |H-Cprev|, |L-Cprev|), then ATR = (ATRprev x 13 + TR) / 14. ATR has EXPANDED again, from midnight's 1,601.65 to 1,633.93 (+2.0%), because the in-progress daily candle has already covered 65,388.0 - 63,610.6 = $1,777 against a completed 2026-07-30 range of $1,541. At 2.56% of spot a normal day now covers about $1,634, which is the arithmetic behind leaving the resting stop at 63,200: that is $609 below spot, roughly a third of an ATR, and it sits below both the 63,313 shelf and the 63,393 4H EMA200.
